security_audit.summary: All static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code formatting. Semantic review found hardcoded tenant identifiers and automated CRM mutation instructions that could alter email and contact records when live Convex access is available. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace fixed IDs with user-supplied parameters and validate tenant scope before every query or mutation.

remediation.issue: Automated CRM and email mutations without approval
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run output and require explicit confirmation before marking emails processed, creating contacts, changing scores, or adding notes.

remediation.issue: Sensitive email handling lacks privacy guidance
remediation.suggestion: Document data retention, consent, and redaction requirements for email bodies, contact notes, and audit logs.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger command execution signatures
remediation.suggestion: Use language-tagged examples and avoid standalone backticks that resemble executable shell blocks.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Tenant Identifiers and Live Data Scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill embeds fixed orgId and workspaceId values while instructing agents to fetch emails and run Convex mutations. A marketplace user with matching access could process or alter a specific tenant workspace.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions repeatedly include concrete orgId and workspaceId values beside email queries and mutations. This is clear tenant-scoping evidence, not a scanner artifact.

semantic_findings.title: Automated CRM Mutations Without Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to mark emails processed, change contact scores, add notes, and log events after a simple trigger. It does not require a dry run or approval before changing CRM records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mutation steps and continue-on-error handling are explicit in the skill text. Legitimate automation is possible, but the missing confirmation step creates a real data integrity risk.

content.user_title: Process CRM Emails with AI Insights
content.value_statement: Teams lose time turning inbound emails into CRM updates. This skill triages unprocessed emails, links contacts, extracts intent, and records audit logs.
actual_capabilities: Fetches unprocessed emails for a specified Unite-Hub workspace.
Extracts sender email addresses and links them to CRM contacts.
Classifies email intent using defined keyword rules.
Labels email sentiment as positive, neutral, or negative.
Updates contact notes, AI scores, processed flags, and audit logs.
limitations: Uses hardcoded org and workspace identifiers in the provided instructions.
Requires compatible Convex queries and mutations to exist.
Does not describe consent checks or manual approval before record updates.
Keyword intent rules may miss nuanced or multilingual messages.

use_cases.title: Triage inbound sales emails
use_cases.description: Convert new email activity into contact records, intent labels, sentiment labels, and follow-up cues.

use_cases.title: Maintain CRM interaction history
use_cases.description: Attach summarized email interactions to contact notes and keep audit records for later review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize warm leads
use_cases.description: Identify contacts with positive sentiment and inquiry intent so teams can focus outreach.

prompt_templates.title: Process New Emails
prompt_templates.prompt: Process unprocessed emails for the configured workspace and summarize the results.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a standard processing pass.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Before Updating
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze unprocessed emails, list detected intents and sentiment, and flag messages that need manual follow-up before updates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when contact data quality matters.

prompt_templates.title: Update Contacts with Audit Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Process new workspace emails, link each sender to a contact, update CRM notes, and include a concise audit summary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for CRM enrichment and traceability.

prompt_templates.title: Run Controlled Processing Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Process up to 20 unprocessed emails, skip ambiguous senders, report contact changes, and identify records needing human review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced controlled run for sensitive workspaces.

output_examples.output: Email processing complete. The agent processed 12 messages, linked 9 contacts, created 3 contacts, and flagged 4 warm leads.

output_examples.input: Analyze unprocessed emails and show follow-up needs.
output_examples.output: The inbox contains pricing requests, partnership inquiries, and one support complaint. Three contacts should receive priority follow-up today.
The sender was linked to an existing contact. The message was positive, had inquiry intent, and added a new CRM note.

best_practices: Run a dry review before allowing record updates in shared workspaces.
Confirm the target org and workspace before processing email batches.
Review high-priority leads after each processing summary.
anti_patterns: Do not run the workflow with hardcoded tenant IDs in a public marketplace setting.
Do not process private email bodies without an approved data handling policy.
Do not rely only on keyword rules for high-value or sensitive customer decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill process?
faq.answer: It processes unprocessed Unite-Hub emails and updates related CRM contact records.

faq.question: Does it create new contacts?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow creates a contact when no matching sender email exists.

faq.question: How does it detect intent?
faq.answer: It uses keyword groups for inquiries, proposals, complaints, questions, follow-ups, and meetings.

faq.question: Does it require database tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects Convex query and mutation tools with access to the target workspace.

faq.question: Can it update production data?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow marks emails processed and updates contact records.

faq.question: What should teams review before use?
faq.answer: Review tenant IDs, access permissions, privacy requirements, and approval steps for CRM mutations.
